topic: How do crosslink requirements in mesh satellite architectures affect feeder link budgets and overall system cost per Mbps?
consensus_response: Crosslink requirements in mesh satellite architectures significantly impact feeder link budgets by increasing power consumption, transmitter size constraints, and signal attenuation due to added complexity. This necessitates careful planning of satellite constellation geometry and inter-satellite link design to minimize interference and maximize capacity. Array factor optimization can mitigate these effects by optimizing satellite antenna gains, while adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) dynamically adjusts coding and modulation schemes based on link conditions. Frequency reuse can also increase capacity while minimizing interference, but introduces additional complexity. Overall, the added complexity of crosslinks negatively impacts feeder link budgets and overall system cost per Mbps.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of power constraints in satellite, ENB, and UE for feasibility of geo and leo feeder and user links, with a focus on array factor optimization, interference analysis, and ACM. It also mentions the need to consider inter-satellite links, routing algorithms, and admission control mechanisms.
